messages.content: A Pune bindery has 45 notebooks. A school collects 17. How many remain on the shelf?
There are 28 notebooks left.
messages.think: Removing the collection leaves 45 - 17 = 28.

messages.content: Sonal buys three metro tickets in Ahmedabad at 34 rupees apiece. What does she pay?
Sonal pays 102 rupees.
messages.think: All three fares match, giving 3 × 34 = 102.

messages.content: Volunteers in Madurai put 56 seed packets into eight hampers equally. What goes in each?
Put 7 seed packets in each hamper.
messages.think: A single hamper gets 56 / 8 = 7 packets.

messages.content: At a Dibrugarh reading room, a film begins at 3:22 and ends at 3:58. Find the running time.
The film runs for 36 minutes.
messages.think: Both times fall within the same hour, so 58 - 22 = 36 minutes pass.

messages.content: A Bhopal teacher keeps 1.3 metres of blue ribbon and 0.65 metres of red ribbon for a display. How much ribbon is available altogether?
There are 1.95 metres of ribbon available.
messages.think: Laid end to end, the ribbons measure 1.3 + 0.65 = 1.95 metres.

messages.content: Jasmeet pays for 160 rupees of vegetables with a 200-rupee note at a Ludhiana market. How much change is due?
Jasmeet should receive 40 rupees in change.
messages.think: The difference between the note and the bill is 200 - 160 = 40.

messages.content: A Salem tailor cuts 250 grams of stuffing from a 2 kg bag. How many grams stay in the bag?
There are 1750 grams of stuffing left.
messages.think:
The untouched bag held 2 × 1000 = 2000 grams.
The new weight is 2000 - 250 = 1750 grams.

messages.content: A seller in Puri puts 15% off a lampshade marked 400 rupees. How much is the discount itself?
The discount is 60 rupees.
messages.think: Apply the discount fraction to the marked price: 400 × 15 / 100 = 60.

messages.content: At a Rajkot club, there are 18 carrom boards upstairs and 14 downstairs. Give the count for the equipment register.
Enter 32 carrom boards in the register.
messages.think: The two floors hold 18 + 14 = 32 boards between them.

messages.content: Mita cycles 760 metres to her tuition class in Siliguri and 440 metres from there to the stationery shop. What is the combined distance in kilometres?
Mita cycles 1.2 kilometres in total.
messages.think:
The two legs add to 760 + 440 = 1200 metres.
In kilometres this is 1200 / 1000 = 1.2.

messages.content: A Hampi guide carries 26 maps. He hands out 8 before lunch and 5 later. How many can he still give away?
He can give away 13 more maps.
messages.think:
The group has already taken 8 + 5 = 13 maps.
The guide still has 26 - 13 = 13.

messages.content: The makerspace in Ranchi charges 18 rupees per badge and 22 rupees for a single order pickup. What will four badges cost with pickup?
The badges and pickup cost 94 rupees.
messages.think:
Making the badges costs 4 × 18 = 72 rupees.
The pickup adds to that bill, making 72 + 22 = 94.

messages.content: Nitin drives at a steady 36 kilometres per hour for 30 minutes on a practice road in Nashik. How far does he go?
Nitin drives 18 kilometres.
messages.think:
The driving time in hours is 30 / 60 = 0.5.
At the stated speed he covers 36 × 0.5 = 18 kilometres.

messages.content: A Lucknow music class runs for 75 minutes. The first exercise takes 28 minutes. How much time is left for the rest?
The class has 47 minutes left.
messages.think: The remaining part of the lesson is 75 - 28 = 47 minutes.

messages.content: For an Onam display, Bindu uses a quarter of the 36 paper leaves she cut. How many go into the display?
Bindu uses 9 paper leaves.
messages.think: One of four equal shares contains 36 / 4 = 9 leaves.

messages.content: At Mysuru bus stand, Kaveri buys tickets for two adults at 48 rupees each and three children at 26 each. What amount should she approve on UPI?
Kaveri should approve 174 rupees.
messages.think:
Adult travel costs 2 × 48 = 96 rupees.
Children's travel costs 3 × 26 = 78 rupees.
The UPI amount is 96 + 78 = 174.

messages.content: A Latur workshop has 7 planks, each 1.6 metres long. The carpenter has used 2.8 metres of their combined length. How many complete 70 cm strips can be made from the remainder if offcuts can be joined without loss?
The carpenter can make 12 complete strips.
messages.think:
The planks together supply 7 × 1.6 = 11.2 metres.
After the earlier work, 11.2 - 2.8 = 8.4 metres remain.
In centimetres the available length is 8.4 × 100 = 840.
That length gives 840 / 70 = 12 strips.

messages.content: A house in Bhuj has a 10 m by 6 m courtyard. A bordered garden takes up a rectangle 4 m by 3 m. Paving costs 110 rupees a square metre. Find the material cost for the open courtyard.
Paving material costs 5280 rupees.
messages.think:
The whole courtyard covers 10 × 6 = 60 square metres.
The garden occupies 4 × 3 = 12 square metres.
Paving is needed over 60 - 12 = 48 square metres.
The material bill is 48 × 110 = 5280 rupees.

messages.content: In Varanasi a guest house charges 1350 rupees a night for two nights and 1500 for the third. The travellers already paid a 600-rupee deposit towards the bill. What balance is due?
The balance due is 3600 rupees.
messages.think:
The first two nights cost 2 × 1350 = 2700 rupees.
All three nights come to 2700 + 1500 = 4200 rupees.
Credit the deposit to find 4200 - 600 = 3600 due.

messages.content: A Patiala grower sells 18 kg of beans at 50 rupees per kg and another 12 kg at 35 rupees per kg. What is the average amount received per kg?
The grower averages 44 rupees per kg.
messages.think:
The higher-priced lot earns 18 × 50 = 900 rupees.
The other lot brings in 12 × 35 = 420 rupees.
Together the lots earn 900 + 420 = 1320 rupees.
The total weight sold is 18 + 12 = 30 kg.
Each kg earns an average of 1320 / 30 = 44 rupees.

messages.content: A school in Chitradurga orders 120 pads. On Monday 30% arrive and on Tuesday 48 more arrive. What percentage is still due?
30% of the order is still due.
messages.think:
Monday's delivery contains 120 × 30 / 100 = 36 pads.
By Tuesday the office has received 36 + 48 = 84.
The supplier still owes 120 - 84 = 36 pads.
Those represent 36 / 120 × 100 = 30 percent of the order.

messages.content: A Surat ferry leaves at 4:47. It takes 23 minutes to reach the far bank and a walk from there takes 19 minutes. When will a passenger finish that walk?
The passenger finishes the walk at 5:29.
messages.think:
The ride and walk take 23 + 19 = 42 minutes.
The first hour changes after 60 - 47 = 13 minutes.
The remaining elapsed time after 5 o'clock is 42 - 13 = 29 minutes.

messages.content: A Cuttack school can pack 14 science kits into each crate. Four full crates are ready and 19 kits await packing. If the last two crates also take 14 each, how many spaces will be empty across all six?
There will be 9 empty kit spaces.
messages.think:
The four packed crates account for 4 × 14 = 56 kits.
Including the pending kits, the shipment contains 56 + 19 = 75.
Six crates can hold 6 × 14 = 84 kits.
Unused places total 84 - 75 = 9.

messages.content: In Kochi, a jeweller sells a silver chain at 20% off its tag price and adds a fixed 120-rupee delivery charge. The customer pays 1720. What did the tag say?
The tag price was 2000 rupees.
messages.think:
The chain alone cost the customer 1720 - 120 = 1600 rupees.
This is 100 - 20 = 80 percent of the marked amount.
Scaling back to the full tag gives 1600 / 80 × 100 = 2000.

messages.content: An Ajmer juice stall starts with 4 litres of lime soda. It serves five 300 ml glasses and spills 100 ml. How many 200 ml glasses can be filled from the remainder?
The stall can fill 12 of the smaller glasses.
messages.think:
In glass units the stall starts with 4 × 1000 = 4000 ml.
Customers drink 5 × 300 = 1500 ml.
After both uses, 4000 - 1500 - 100 = 2400 ml remains.
The smaller glasses each take 200 ml, giving 2400 / 200 = 12 full glasses.

messages.content: A Kabaddi club in Panipat begins with 480 rupees in its shared wallet. Four copies of its rulebook cost 65 rupees each. A supplier returns 35 rupees from an earlier purchase. What will the wallet show?
The wallet will show 255 rupees.
messages.think:
The new books reduce the wallet by 4 × 65 = 260 rupees.
Before the refund it holds 480 - 260 = 220 rupees.
The credit raises the balance to 220 + 35 = 255.

messages.content: Summit school in Shimla has a rectangular play area 18 m long and 11 m wide. It needs a rope around the edge except for an opening of 4 m. How long should the rope be?
A 54-metre rope will cover the required edge.
messages.think:
One long and one short edge together measure 18 + 11 = 29 metres.
The whole boundary measures 2 × 29 = 58 metres.
The gap reduces the rope needed to 58 - 4 = 54 metres.

messages.content: A bhel stand in Nagpur sells a small portion for 25 rupees and a large one for 40. A group orders 7 small and 4 large portions. It pays with 500 rupees. How much change?
The group should get 165 rupees back.
messages.think:
The small portions contribute 7 × 25 = 175 rupees to the bill.
The large orders contribute 4 × 40 = 160 rupees.
The vendor needs 175 + 160 = 335 rupees.
The balance of the note is 500 - 335 = 165.

messages.content: Two vans carry 28 and 32 players to a tournament in Kolhapur. Six players from the first van and four from the second stay for a later session. How many are in the current session?
50 players are in the current session.
messages.think:
The vans deliver 28 + 32 = 60 players.
The later session has 6 + 4 = 10 of them.
That leaves 60 - 10 = 50 in the current session.

messages.content: Meera in Bokaro has 2.4 kg of flour and borrows 350 grams from a neighbour. Her recipe uses 1.75 kg. How many grams does she have after baking?
Meera has 1000 grams of flour left.
messages.think:
Meera's own flour weighs 2.4 × 1000 = 2400 grams.
With the borrowed flour the total is 2400 + 350 = 2750 grams.
The recipe takes 1.75 × 1000 = 1750 grams.
The remainder weighs 2750 - 1750 = 1000 grams.

messages.content: A library in Gaya packs 5 cartons with 22 books per carton. Six books have torn pages and must be pulled out. The intact books go onto shelves holding 13 each. How many shelves are filled?
8 shelves are filled.
messages.think:
The cartons start with 5 × 22 = 110 books.
Removing damaged stock gives 110 - 6 = 104 books.
The shelf count is 104 / 13 = 8.

messages.content: A Chandigarh caterer has 42 plates. She lends one-third to a neighbour, then borrows 9 from her sister. How many can she use tonight?
She can use 37 plates tonight.
messages.think:
The neighbour takes 42 / 3 = 14 plates.
After the loan her own stock is 42 - 14 = 28.
Her sister's plates raise the available count to 28 + 9 = 37.

messages.content: A Kottayam school quiz awards 7 points per correct answer and deducts 3 for each wrong answer. Blank responses carry no points. Joel gets 9 right, 4 wrong and leaves 2 blank. What is his score?
Joel scores 51 points.
messages.think:
Joel earns 9 × 7 = 63 points from correct answers.
His mistakes cost 4 × 3 = 12 points.
With blanks unchanged, the score is 63 - 12 = 51.

messages.content: A Mysuru pottery shop wants to finish 84 cups in eight days. It finishes 15 a day for the first three days and 11 on the fourth. How many cups should it make per day across the final four days?
The shop should make 7 cups per day.
messages.think:
Three days account for 3 × 15 = 45 cups.
The fourth brings the count to 45 + 11 = 56.
The remaining target is 84 - 56 = 28 cups.
Splitting that equally over four days gives 28 / 4 = 7.

messages.content: An Indore photo shop sells 25 prints at 8 rupees each. Five prints are blurry, and their full print charges are refunded. The customer also buys a replacement sleeve for 18 rupees. What is the net spend?
The customer spends 178 rupees in total.
messages.think:
The original print charge is 25 × 8 = 200 rupees.
The shop returns 5 × 8 = 40 rupees.
The customer ultimately pays 200 - 40 = 160 for the prints.
Add the sleeve to get 160 + 18 = 178 rupees.

messages.content: A group in Shillong can hire three bicycles at 75 rupees each and one tandem at 120 rupees. A guide costs 95 rupees. They collect 500 rupees. What is left for snacks?
The group has 60 rupees left for snacks.
messages.think:
The ordinary bicycles cost 3 × 75 = 225 rupees.
Vehicle hire plus the guide totals 225 + 120 + 95 = 440.
The snack fund is 500 - 440 = 60 rupees.

messages.content: At a Dussehra fair in Bareilly, a stall has 65 masks. Twelve are kept for a school. The rest are arranged in packets of five. How many full packets and loose masks are there?
There are 10 full packets and 3 loose masks.
messages.think:
The fair stock is 65 - 12 = 53 masks.
Ten full packets take 10 × 5 = 50 masks.
There are 53 - 50 = 3 left, too few for another packet.

messages.content: At a Kalaburagi warehouse, an empty sack weighs 1.5 kg and a full one 26.5 kg. There are eight full sacks. If 20 kg of their contents is set aside, what is available to dispatch?
180 kg is available to dispatch.
messages.think:
Contents per sack weigh 26.5 - 1.5 = 25 kg.
All the sacks contain 8 × 25 = 200 kg of goods.
The dispatch load is 200 - 20 = 180 kg.

messages.content: A Guntur gardener buys seedlings in trays of 16. She needs 88 plants and already has 28. How many trays must she buy at a minimum, and how many seedlings will be spare?
She needs 4 trays and will have 4 seedlings spare.
messages.think:
The gardener is short by 88 - 28 = 60 plants.
Three trays would supply 3 × 16 = 48, which falls short.
Four trays provide 4 × 16 = 64 seedlings.
The spare count is 64 - 60 = 4.

messages.content: At an evening cricket match in Jamshedpur, a team needs 138 runs to win. It has 87 at the end of 12 overs and scores 15 in the next over. The innings lasts 19 overs. What run rate is needed from here?
The team needs 6 runs per over.
messages.think:
The latest over brings the score to 87 + 15 = 102.
The team has completed 12 + 1 = 13 overs.
It can still bat for 19 - 13 = 6 overs.
To win it needs 138 - 102 = 36 more runs.
The required rate is 36 / 6 = 6 runs per over.

messages.content: A book fair in Thrissur sells 48 books at 150 rupees each. A sponsor pays 30% of the venue charge, which is 3000 rupees. The books cost the organiser 85 rupees each, and transport cost 420 rupees. How much does the organiser retain?
The organiser retains 600 rupees.
messages.think:
Sales bring in 48 × 150 = 7200 rupees.
Buying the books costs 48 × 85 = 4080 rupees.
The sponsor covers 3000 × 30 / 100 = 900 rupees.
The organiser's venue share is 3000 - 900 = 2100 rupees.
Including transport, the organiser pays 4080 + 2100 + 420 = 6600 rupees.
The money retained is 7200 - 6600 = 600 rupees.

messages.content: In Nanded, the art room starts with 144 red tiles and 96 white ones. One-sixth of the red tiles and one-quarter of the white tiles crack. The intact tiles all go in panels, each using 5 red and 3 white tiles. How many panels can the teachers finish, and are any intact tiles left?
The teachers can finish 24 panels with no intact tiles left over.
messages.think:
The cracked red count is 144 / 6 = 24.
The cracked white count is 96 / 4 = 24.
Intact red tiles number 144 - 24 = 120.
Intact white tiles number 96 - 24 = 72.
Red tiles are sufficient for 120 / 5 = 24 panels.
White tiles likewise cover 72 / 3 = 24 panels.
The spare red count is 120 - 24 × 5 = 0.
The spare white count is 72 - 24 × 3 = 0.

messages.content: A cobbler in Udupi sees 18 customers in the first three days of the week on average per day. The count for Wednesday was recorded as 14 instead of 20. Thursday and Friday have 25 and 22 customers. She wants an average of 22 for the six days through Saturday. How many customers must she see on Saturday?
She must see 25 customers on Saturday.
messages.think:
The book lists 3 × 18 = 54 customers for the first three days.
Wednesday's missing customers number 20 - 14 = 6.
The corrected count for those days is 54 + 6 = 60.
Friday's closing count for the five days is 60 + 25 + 22 = 107.
The six-day goal corresponds to 6 × 22 = 132 customers.
Saturday must account for 132 - 107 = 25.

messages.content: A festival stall in Rourkela orders 9 strings of 24 paper lanterns. On arrival, 12 are damaged. The stall gives one-third of the intact lanterns to a school and sells the remainder in sets of four. The total received from set sales is 4080 rupees. What is the price of a set?
Each set costs 120 rupees.
messages.think:
The delivery starts with 9 × 24 = 216 lanterns.
The intact supply is 216 - 12 = 204.
The school receives 204 / 3 = 68 lanterns.
That leaves 204 - 68 = 136 for sale.
The stall sells 136 / 4 = 34 sets.
A set therefore costs 4080 / 34 = 120 rupees.

messages.content: A Surat fabric shop lists a roll for 3600 rupees. Rukmini gets 10% off, and the shop then gives her 5% off the reduced price. She pays 72 rupees for delivery and shares the fabric and total bill equally with two friends. How much does Rukmini pay?
Rukmini pays 1050 rupees.
messages.think:
The first cut is 3600 × 10 / 100 = 360 rupees.
The roll goes down to 3600 - 360 = 3240 rupees.
The second discount is based on 3240, giving 3240 × 5 / 100 = 162 rupees.
The cloth then costs 3240 - 162 = 3078 rupees.
The delivered bill comes to 3078 + 72 = 3150 rupees.
Each of the three buyers contributes 3150 / 3 = 1050 rupees.

messages.content: A Bhopal sports club has an 18 m by 12 m practice area and a 9 m by 8 m warm-up area. A 6 m by 6 m section of the practice area already has new flooring. The club will tile the remaining area at 4 tiles per square metre and buy extra tiles equal to 5% of the number needed. How many tiles should it order?
The club should order 1059 tiles.
messages.think:
The entire practice area measures 18 × 12 = 216 square metres.
The warm-up area measures 9 × 8 = 72 square metres.
The already finished section measures 6 × 6 = 36 square metres.
The area awaiting tiles totals 216 + 72 - 36 = 252 square metres.
Fitting that area takes 252 × 4 = 1008 tiles.
The allowance is 1008 × 5 / 100 = 50.4 tiles, so 51 whole extras are needed to reach at least 5%.
The order is 1008 + 51 = 1059 tiles.

messages.content: At a Delhi community kitchen, two cooks pack 18 and 22 meals per hour. The faster cook arrives an hour late. They work together for 2 hours, then stop for a 30-minute break. After the break only the faster cook returns, and the kitchen needs 142 meals in all. How much time passes from the first cook's start to the last meal?
The last meal is ready 5.5 hours after the first cook starts.
messages.think:
The first cook packs 1 × 18 = 18 meals before the second arrives.
Working together they pack 18 + 22 = 40 meals per hour.
Before the break they add 2 × 40 = 80 meals.
The last stint must cover 142 - 18 - 80 = 44 meals.
At the faster cook's rate it takes 44 / 22 = 2 hours.
The break is 30 / 60 = 0.5 hours.
The time from start to finish is 1 + 2 + 0.5 + 2 = 5.5 hours.

messages.content: A school in Pune hires two coaches with 36 seats each and one van with 12 seats. Ten of the vehicle seats are reserved for staff. Of the 78 children who signed up, 6 cancel. A coach costs 2200 rupees and the van costs 1200. The school contributes 560 rupees and the travelling children split the rest. What do they pay each, and how many seats are spare?
Each pupil pays 70 rupees, and 2 seats are spare.
messages.think:
The vehicles provide 2 × 36 + 12 = 84 seats.
The pupil capacity is 84 - 10 = 74 seats.
The trip now has 78 - 6 = 72 pupils.
There are 74 - 72 = 2 spare seats.
The coach hire totals 2 × 2200 = 4400 rupees.
Including the van, hire comes to 4400 + 1200 = 5600 rupees.
After the school's contribution, pupils owe 5600 - 560 = 5040 rupees.
A pupil's share is 5040 / 72 = 70 rupees.

messages.content: At a Kolkata stall, 2.4 litres of mango drink contains 25% mango juice. Another 1.2 litres contains 50%. The stall mixes them and adds 400 ml of water. Assuming volumes add directly, what share of the final drink is mango juice?
The final drink contains 30% mango juice.
messages.think:
The first jug holds 2.4 × 1000 = 2400 ml of drink.
Its juice content is 2400 × 25 / 100 = 600 ml.
The second jug holds 1.2 × 1000 = 1200 ml of drink.
It contributes 1200 × 50 / 100 = 600 ml of juice.
The two lots contribute 600 + 600 = 1200 ml of juice.
After adding water the final drink measures 2400 + 1200 + 400 = 4000 ml.
Its percentage of juice is 1200 / 4000 × 100 = 30.

messages.content: A Madurai tailor receives 18 metres of cotton at 120 rupees per metre. She uses 1.4 metres each for 10 shirts and 2 metres for samples. The supplier buys back the remaining fabric at 75% of the original rate. She sells all the shirts for 290 rupees each and pays 340 rupees for buttons and thread. What amount is left after these expenses?
The tailor has 580 rupees left after those expenses.
messages.think:
The original cloth costs 18 × 120 = 2160 rupees.
Shirt cutting uses 10 × 1.4 = 14 metres.
After the samples the returnable length is 18 - 14 - 2 = 2 metres.
The supplier pays 120 × 75 / 100 = 90 rupees per metre returned.
The return brings in 2 × 90 = 180 rupees.
Shirt sales add 10 × 290 = 2900 rupees.
The total outlay is 2160 + 340 = 2500 rupees.
What remains is 180 + 2900 - 2500 = 580 rupees.

messages.content: At a school in Kolar, 38 puppets go on display and 14 stay in the cupboard. How many puppets does the school have?
The school has 52 puppets.
messages.think: The cupboard and display together hold 38 + 14 = 52.

messages.content: A group in Agra buys five 19-rupee postcards to send home. What does the shop collect?
The shop collects 95 rupees.
messages.think: The price is the same for every card, giving 5 × 19 = 95.

messages.content: The florist in Panaji needs to arrange 54 stems in six identical bunches. How many stems belong in each bunch?
Put 9 stems in each bunch.
messages.think: Each of the six bunches receives 54 / 6 = 9 stems.

messages.content: A pottery demonstration in Bhuj runs from 10:24 to 10:53. How long does the audience watch?
The audience watches for 29 minutes.
messages.think: Within the 10 o'clock hour, the gap is 53 - 24 = 29 minutes.

messages.content: A home cook in Shillong combines 0.75 litres of coconut milk with 1.2 litres of stock. What volume goes into the pan if the volumes add directly?
The pan receives 1.95 litres.
messages.think: The two liquids give 0.75 + 1.2 = 1.95 litres.

messages.content: A Mitra Mandal has 63 banners, and 8 have torn at the corners. How many are still intact?
There are 55 intact banners.
messages.think: Leave out the damaged ones to get 63 - 8 = 55.

messages.content: Nida buys 2.6 kg of gram flour in Surat. She uses 750 grams. Find the weight left in grams.
Nida has 1850 grams left.
messages.think:
The original purchase weighs 2.6 × 1000 = 2600 grams.
After cooking, the bag contains 2600 - 750 = 1850 grams.

messages.content: An art shop in Hazaribagh offers 12% off a frame marked 650 rupees. What is the saving?
The saving is 78 rupees.
messages.think: The saving is the stated share of the tag, 650 × 12 / 100 = 78.

messages.content: Rupa pays 300 rupees to a Patna vendor for a lamp costing 248 rupees. What change should she get?
Rupa should get 52 rupees back.
messages.think: The excess over the lamp price is 300 - 248 = 52.

messages.content: A volunteer walks 520 metres from his home to the ward office in Kochi, then another 730 metres to the jetty. How far is that in kilometres?
He walks 1.25 kilometres.
messages.think:
The two walks cover 520 + 730 = 1250 metres.
Expressed in kilometres, that is 1250 / 1000 = 1.25.

messages.content: A repair shop in Thanjavur has 41 locks waiting for testing. Twelve passed in the morning and seven in the afternoon. How many still need testing if no locks failed?
22 locks still need testing.
messages.think:
So far 12 + 7 = 19 passed.
The awaiting stock is 41 - 19 = 22 locks.

messages.content: Three idlis cost 11 rupees each at a Mangaluru stall. Sahana adds chutney for 9 rupees. What does she owe?
Sahana owes 42 rupees.
messages.think:
Her idlis cost 3 × 11 = 33 rupees.
The additional chutney makes the bill 33 + 9 = 42.

messages.content: A maker in Aizawl reserves one-sixth of a batch of 72 buttons for repairs. How many go into the repair tin?
Put 12 buttons in the repair tin.
messages.think: The reserved portion contains 72 / 6 = 12 buttons.

messages.content: An assembly in Mhow lasts 55 minutes. When the first speaker sits down, 21 minutes have passed. How long is left?
The assembly has 34 minutes left.
messages.think: The remaining time is 55 - 21 = 34 minutes.

messages.content: A veranda table in Cuttack measures 1.8 metres by 0.5 metres. What area will an exactly fitting cover occupy?
The cover occupies 0.9 square metres.
messages.think: Multiply the two dimensions to get 1.8 × 0.5 = 0.9 square metres.

messages.content: In Jalgaon, Neel orders 3 trays of 16 saplings. Six wilt before planting. The workers lay out rows of 7. How many complete rows can they plant?
The workers can plant 6 complete rows.
messages.think:
The order contains 3 × 16 = 48 saplings.
Removing the wilted ones leaves 48 - 6 = 42 to plant.
The layout allows 42 / 7 = 6 rows.

messages.content: Dilshad leaves a clinic in Moradabad at 6:48. The chemist takes 14 minutes and the walk home takes 19 more. When does Dilshad arrive, assuming there is no other delay?
Dilshad arrives at 7:21.
messages.think:
The two activities take 14 + 19 = 33 minutes.
Seven o'clock comes after 60 - 48 = 12 minutes.
The walk ends 33 - 12 = 21 minutes into the next hour.

messages.content: A Churu shop marks a wall clock at 1250 rupees. It takes 16% off and charges 45 rupees for delivery. What goes on the receipt?
The receipt totals 1095 rupees.
messages.think:
The discount comes to 1250 × 16 / 100 = 200 rupees.
The lower price is 1250 - 200 = 1050 rupees.
Delivery makes the amount payable 1050 + 45 = 1095.

messages.content: A Rajahmundry club has 450 rupees on its travel card. It spends 4 fares at 62 rupees each and gets a 30-rupee credit from an earlier trip. Find the new balance.
The travel card now holds 232 rupees.
messages.think:
The fares use 4 × 62 = 248 rupees.
Until the credit arrives the card holds 450 - 248 = 202 rupees.
The credited amount raises this to 202 + 30 = 232.

messages.content: A Buxar wholesaler owes a school 240 exercise books. He brings 20% in the morning and another 84 by dusk. What percentage is still outstanding?
45% of the order is outstanding.
messages.think:
The first batch is 240 × 20 / 100 = 48 books.
The school now has 48 + 84 = 132 books from the order.
It still needs 240 - 132 = 108.
As a share of the order, the shortfall is 108 / 240 × 100 = 45 percent.

messages.content: A music school in Dharwad has 60 instruments, with flutes and drums in the ratio 3:2. It lends 8 drums to a troupe. How many drums stay at the school?
16 drums stay at the school.
messages.think:
There are 3 + 2 = 5 equal shares in the ratio.
Each share represents 60 / 5 = 12 instruments.
The school starts with 2 × 12 = 24 drums.
The loan leaves 24 - 8 = 16 drums.

messages.content: The wall of a Veraval storeroom is 7 metres wide and 4 metres high. Leave a 2 m by 1.5 m window unpainted. At 52 rupees per square metre, what will the paint work cost?
The paint work costs 1300 rupees.
messages.think:
The complete rectangle measures 7 × 4 = 28 square metres.
The window occupies 2 × 1.5 = 3 square metres.
The crew paints 28 - 3 = 25 square metres.
At the quoted rate, the charge is 25 × 52 = 1300 rupees.

messages.content: A Kohima stall pays 70 rupees per kg for 9 kg of ginger and 55 rupees per kg for another 6 kg. What was the average rate over the purchase?
The average rate was 64 rupees per kg.
messages.think:
The first lot costs 9 × 70 = 630 rupees.
The second costs 6 × 55 = 330 rupees.
The combined payment is 630 + 330 = 960.
The combined weight is 9 + 6 = 15 kg.
That works out to 960 / 15 = 64 rupees per kg.

messages.content: There are 52 excursion participants in Gadag. Two 19-seat vans fill up. The remaining people board a van with 17 seats. How many seats are empty?
The last van has 3 empty seats.
messages.think:
The full vans take 2 × 19 = 38 participants.
The last van takes 52 - 38 = 14 people.
Its vacancy count is 17 - 14 = 3.

messages.content: A 600-litre tank at a Rewa school holds 215 litres. A tap adds 26 litres each minute for five minutes, and cleaners then use 65 litres. How much more water would fill it?
It takes another 320 litres to fill the tank.
messages.think:
The tap delivers 5 × 26 = 130 litres.
Before cleaning, the tank holds 215 + 130 = 345 litres.
After cleaning it holds 345 - 65 = 280 litres.
Filling the rest takes 600 - 280 = 320 litres.

messages.content: An art festival in Nashik charges 79 rupees for a day pass and 315 for access on five days. A visitor will attend on four days. Which pass arrangement costs less, and by how much?
Buy the five-day pass to save 1 rupee.
messages.think:
The longer pass leaves 5 - 4 = 1 day unused.
Four separate passes cost 4 × 79 = 316 rupees.
The saving on the five-day pass is 316 - 315 = 1 rupee.

messages.content: An embroidery group in Burhanpur is making 114 patches in six days. It makes 18 daily for the first three days and 20 on day four. How many should it make on each remaining day if both days have the same target?
The group should make 20 patches on each remaining day.
messages.think:
The first three days produce 3 × 18 = 54 patches.
Day four brings progress to 54 + 20 = 74.
There are 114 - 74 = 40 patches to go.
The two daily targets are equal, so 40 / 2 = 20.

messages.content: An invoice in Bareilly totals 2380 rupees including 140 rupees for delivery. A 20% discount was applied to the table itself. What was the original table price?
The table was originally priced at 2800 rupees.
messages.think:
The customer paid 2380 - 140 = 2240 rupees for the table.
The invoice charges 100 - 20 = 80 percent of the marked price for it.
Scaling up gives 2240 / 80 × 100 = 2800.

messages.content: The community hall in Hisar needs 173 paper lantern hooks. A volunteer finds boxes holding 31 and 52 hooks. The shop sells 18 to a packet. How many packets should she buy?
She should buy 5 packets.
messages.think:
The two boxes provide 31 + 52 = 83 hooks.
The remaining requirement is 173 - 83 = 90.
For shop packets, 90 / 18 = 5.

messages.content: A driver in Kullu covers 45 km in the first 1.5 hours and 95 km in the next 2.5 hours. What is the average speed across both legs?
The average speed is 35 km per hour.
messages.think:
Over the two legs the car travels 45 + 95 = 140 km.
The combined driving time is 1.5 + 2.5 = 4 hours.
The average works out to 140 / 4 = 35 km per hour.

messages.content: Three friends in Puducherry split a 1080-rupee room and a 210-rupee ride. Each also buys a 95-rupee entry ticket. What does each spend?
Each friend spends 525 rupees.
messages.think:
The entry tickets cost 3 × 95 = 285 rupees in all.
The group's complete spend is 1080 + 210 + 285 = 1575.
Dividing among the three gives 1575 / 3 = 525.

messages.content: A Dhanbad spelling round gives 6 points for each right answer and subtracts 2 for each wrong answer. Skips are worth zero. Sameer answers 14 correctly, gets 5 wrong and skips one. What does he score?
Sameer scores 74 points.
messages.think:
Sameer's correct answers earn 14 × 6 = 84 points.
The mistakes cost 5 × 2 = 10 points.
The skipped word has no effect, so his score is 84 - 10 = 74.

messages.content: A tea seller is sixth in a queue at an RTO counter in Sambalpur. The counter opens in 8 minutes and each earlier customer will take 7 minutes. When will the seller's turn begin?
The seller's turn will begin in 43 minutes.
messages.think:
Earlier places in line number 6 - 1 = 5.
Serving those customers will take 5 × 7 = 35 minutes.
Counting the time before opening, the wait is 8 + 35 = 43 minutes.

messages.content: A community pantry in Dibrugarh starts with 6 kg of rice. A cook uses 950 grams at lunch and 1.4 kg at dinner. How many grams remain?
3650 grams of rice remain.
messages.think:
The pantry starts with 6 × 1000 = 6000 grams.
Dinner takes 1.4 × 1000 = 1400 grams.
Both meals use 950 + 1400 = 2350 grams.
The pantry still has 6000 - 2350 = 3650 grams.

messages.content: In Nagercoil, seven fruit crates weigh 23 kg each when filled and 1 kg each empty. A vendor sets aside 14 kg of the fruit. What weight can she sell?
She can sell 140 kg of fruit.
messages.think:
The fruit content of each crate is 23 - 1 = 22 kg.
The whole delivery contains 7 × 22 = 154 kg of fruit.
After putting aside her share she can sell 154 - 14 = 140 kg.

messages.content: A Bolpur team is chasing 158 in 18 overs. It is on 96 after 11 overs and then scores 14 in the next over. At what average rate must it score now?
The team needs 8 runs per over.
messages.think:
The team has moved to 96 + 14 = 110 runs.
Overs used are 11 + 1 = 12.
The team can still bat for 18 - 12 = 6 overs.
To win it needs 158 - 110 = 48 more runs.
That means 48 / 6 = 8 runs per over.

messages.content: Around a 19 m by 13 m garden in Hoshiarpur there will be rope except for a 5 m opening. How much rope should the gardener bring?
The gardener should bring 59 metres of rope.
messages.think:
Two adjacent sides measure 19 + 13 = 32 metres.
The full rectangle has a perimeter of 2 × 32 = 64 metres.
Leaving the entry open requires 64 - 5 = 59 metres.

messages.content: An Idukki stall makes 89 biscuits. Seven go to the organisers. The rest are put into packs of 9. How many complete packs are there and how many biscuits are loose?
There are 9 complete packs and 1 loose biscuit.
messages.think:
The organisers leave 89 - 7 = 82 biscuits for the stall.
Nine full packs take 9 × 9 = 81 biscuits.
There are 82 - 81 = 1 loose biscuit, too few for another pack.

messages.content: A hotel in Guntur charges 680 rupees each for the first two nights and 760 for the last night. Priyanka already paid a 500-rupee deposit. What must she pay now?
Priyanka must pay 1620 rupees now.
messages.think:
The first part of the stay comes to 2 × 680 = 1360 rupees.
For all the nights the hotel charges 1360 + 760 = 2120 rupees.
Applying the deposit leaves 2120 - 500 = 1620 due.

messages.content: Nine drawing pads at 35 rupees each and four erasers at 12 rupees each go on Anu's bill in Bagalkot. The shop refunds the full price of two damaged pads. What is her net payment?
Anu pays 293 rupees in the end.
messages.think:
The original pad charge is 9 × 35 = 315 rupees.
Erasers add 4 × 12 = 48 rupees.
The shop returns 2 × 35 = 70 rupees.
After the refund, her payment is 315 + 48 - 70 = 293.

messages.content: The craft club at a Rohtak school gets 96 red and 100 blue beads. It keeps one-quarter of the red and 10% of the blue for a later event. Each key ring uses four red and five blue beads. After making as many rings as possible, the club sells them at 40 rupees each. Each ring also needs a clasp bought for 6 rupees. How much does the club collect after paying for the clasps?
The club collects 612 rupees after paying for the clasps.
messages.think:
The later event gets 96 / 4 = 24 red beads.
The red beads available now number 96 - 24 = 72.
The club puts aside 100 × 10 / 100 = 10 blue beads.
That leaves 100 - 10 = 90 blue beads.
The red supply covers 72 / 4 = 18 rings.
The blue supply also covers 90 / 5 = 18 rings.
Each completed ring brings in 40 - 6 = 34 rupees after its clasp.
The collection after clasps is 18 × 34 = 612 rupees.

messages.content: At the Thrissur fair, a bus will charge a group 40 rupees per adult and 25 per child. There are 18 adults and 24 children, but 4 of the children have vouchers that cover their fares. The bus operator adds 180 rupees for a stop at the fairground. The organiser has 500 rupees of donations for the trip. How much more must the organiser raise?
The organiser must raise another 900 rupees.
messages.think:
The adults account for 18 × 40 = 720 rupees.
The number of children needing paid fares is 24 - 4 = 20.
Their fares add 20 × 25 = 500 rupees.
The total fare after vouchers is 720 + 500 = 1220 rupees.
The extra stop makes the bill 1220 + 180 = 1400 rupees.
Donations leave 1400 - 500 = 900 rupees to raise.

messages.content: In Puducherry, a hostel wants 210 clean sheets ready by noon. Fathima folds 18 sheets per hour and works alone for 2 hours before Arun joins at 24 sheets per hour. The pair works for 3 hours, then takes a 15-minute tea break. After that Arun folds the remaining sheets alone. How many hours after Fathima started is the stack ready?
The stack is ready 7.25 hours after Fathima starts.
messages.think:
Fathima folds 2 × 18 = 36 sheets on her own.
The pair works at 18 + 24 = 42 sheets per hour.
They add 3 × 42 = 126 sheets before their break.
The count still to be folded is 210 - 36 - 126 = 48.
Arun's solo period lasts 48 / 24 = 2 hours.
The break lasts 15 / 60 = 0.25 hours.
The elapsed time is 2 + 3 + 0.25 + 2 = 7.25 hours.

messages.content: At a Kozhikode stall, a 1.5-litre batch of drink is 20% pineapple juice. A second batch of 750 ml is 50% juice. The stall pours both into a jug, then adds 450 ml of water. If the volumes add directly, what percentage of the new drink is pineapple juice?
The drink is 25% pineapple juice.
messages.think:
The larger batch measures 1.5 × 1000 = 1500 ml.
Its pineapple juice is 1500 × 20 / 100 = 300 ml.
The smaller batch contributes 750 × 50 / 100 = 375 ml of juice.
The jug therefore contains 300 + 375 = 675 ml of pineapple juice.
Water brings the total drink to 1500 + 750 + 450 = 2700 ml.
The juice share is 675 / 2700 × 100 = 25 percent.

messages.content: A housing society in Nagpur has a 25 m by 16 m roof. A 20 m by 3 m strip and a separate 5 m by 4 m shed must remain untouched. Waterproofing gel covers 8 square metres per litre. The society needs 10% extra gel and buys it in 4.4-litre drums. How many drums does it need?
The society needs 10 drums of gel.
messages.think:
The roof area is 25 × 16 = 400 square metres.
The strip accounts for 20 × 3 = 60 square metres.
The shed accounts for 5 × 4 = 20 square metres.
The area to cover is 400 - 60 - 20 = 320 square metres.
The regular dose is 320 / 8 = 40 litres.
The extra gel is 40 × 10 / 100 = 4 litres.
The full quantity is 40 + 4 = 44 litres.
The society needs 44 / 4.4 = 10 drums.

messages.content: Three friends order a weaving kit from Bhagalpur. The kit is marked 3800 rupees, with 10% off and then another 5% off the reduced price. Delivery costs 111 rupees. One friend has already paid a 360-rupee deposit from the group's shared fund. What amount must each friend contribute if they split only the unpaid balance equally?
Each friend must contribute 1000 rupees toward the balance.
messages.think:
The first saving is 3800 × 10 / 100 = 380 rupees.
That leaves a kit price of 3800 - 380 = 3420.
The second saving is 3420 × 5 / 100 = 171 rupees.
The discounted kit costs 3420 - 171 = 3249 rupees.
Adding the courier brings the bill to 3249 + 111 = 3360.
Applying the deposit leaves 3360 - 360 = 3000.
An equal share of the balance is 3000 / 3 = 1000 rupees.

messages.content: An auditorium in Mysuru has 12 rows of 18 chairs. The crew takes out three rows to make room for a camera and puts 4 rows of 12 chairs down one side. It reserves 18 chairs for organisers. The other 240 guests can use the remaining chairs or sit on 6-person benches. How many benches should be brought in?
Bring in 8 benches.
messages.think:
The original layout has 12 × 18 = 216 chairs.
Making space for the camera removes 3 × 18 = 54 chairs.
The original block now has 216 - 54 = 162 chairs.
The side rows supply 4 × 12 = 48 more.
The changed layout holds 162 + 48 = 210 chairs.
After reserving the organisers' seats, 210 - 18 = 192 are free for guests.
The bench section must seat 240 - 192 = 48 guests.
That takes 48 / 6 = 8 benches.

messages.content: A Goa homestay offers three nights at 1500 rupees per night, with a 12% discount on the room charge. Six breakfasts cost 135 rupees apiece. A refundable 500-rupee key deposit is collected. At checkout the host returns 420 rupees and keeps the rest for a lost key. How much did the stay ultimately cost?
The stay ultimately costs 4850 rupees.
messages.think:
The room charge starts at 3 × 1500 = 4500 rupees.
The accommodation discount is 4500 × 12 / 100 = 540 rupees.
After the discount the room costs 4500 - 540 = 3960.
Breakfasts add 6 × 135 = 810 rupees.
The part of the deposit retained is 500 - 420 = 80 rupees.
Including that charge, the stay costs 3960 + 810 + 80 = 4850.

messages.content: The Sikar municipal library used 275 electricity units last month. Its contract charges 4 rupees per unit for the first 80 units, 7 for the next 120 and 9 for the rest. This month it receives a 250-rupee credit against that bill but pays a 125-rupee standing charge and a 75-rupee late fee. What is due?
The library owes 1785 rupees.
messages.think:
The base band costs 80 × 4 = 320 rupees.
The next band costs 120 × 7 = 840 rupees.
The remaining usage is 275 - 80 - 120 = 75 units.
That band adds 75 × 9 = 675 rupees.
The charges before the credit total 320 + 840 + 675 + 125 + 75 = 2035 rupees.
After applying the credit, 2035 - 250 = 1785 remains due.

messages.content: In Sagar, Tejal buys okra for 63 rupees and pays with a 100-rupee note. What change is due?
Tejal should receive 37 rupees.
messages.think: The excess over the vegetable bill is 100 - 63 = 37.

messages.content: A Dindigul parcel room has eight trays with 13 key blanks apiece. How many blanks are ready?
104 key blanks are ready.
messages.think: The trays together hold 8 × 13 = 104.

messages.content: At a Basti primary school, 84 counters must be split evenly among six tables. How many go on each?
Put 14 counters on each table.
messages.think: Each table takes an equal share of 84 / 6 = 14.

messages.content: A clay demonstration in Bankura starts at 10:13 and ends at 10:41. What is its length?
The demonstration lasts 28 minutes.
messages.think: Within the same hour, 41 - 13 = 28 minutes pass.

messages.content: A kitchen in Palakkad combines 1.15 litres of stock and 0.85 litres of water. What is the total volume if the liquids add directly?
The kitchen has 2 litres of liquid.
messages.think: The combined measure is 1.15 + 0.85 = 2 litres.

messages.content: An umbrella tagged 460 rupees is 15% off at a Pune shop. What amount does the discount take off?
The discount takes off 69 rupees.
messages.think: The tag is reduced by 460 × 15 / 100 = 69.

messages.content: A baker in Kohima uses 450 grams from a 2.7 kg bag of flour. How many grams are left?
2250 grams of flour are left.
messages.think:
The bag starts with 2.7 × 1000 = 2700 grams.
The remaining flour weighs 2700 - 450 = 2250 grams.

messages.content: For a Ganesh festival notice board, 18 photos arrive in the morning and 23 after lunch. How many have arrived?
41 photos have arrived.
messages.think: The two deliveries contain 18 + 23 = 41 photos.

messages.content: Rafi walks 580 metres to the canal at Alappuzha and another 670 metres to the jetty. How far has he walked in kilometres?
Rafi has walked 1.25 kilometres.
messages.think:
The full walk is 580 + 670 = 1250 metres.
Converting to kilometres gives 1250 / 1000 = 1.25.

messages.content: At a tea stall in Tezpur, four teas cost 16 rupees each. A shared plate of toast costs 21 rupees. What is the bill?
The bill is 85 rupees.
messages.think:
The tea costs 4 × 16 = 64 rupees.
Toast makes the total 64 + 21 = 85.

messages.content: A silversmith in Cuttack has 62 clasps awaiting inspection. He has already checked 38. How many must he still check?
He must still check 24 clasps.
messages.think: The unchecked count is 62 - 38 = 24.

messages.content: A Kumbakonam florist puts one-eighth of her 72 lotus buds aside for a temple. What is the temple's share?
The temple's share is 9 lotus buds.
messages.think: One of eight equal shares contains 72 / 8 = 9 buds.

messages.content: An exact-fit sheet is needed for a notice board 2.4 metres wide and 0.75 metres tall in Kurukshetra. What is the area of the sheet?
The sheet must cover 1.8 square metres.
messages.think: The rectangle covers 2.4 × 0.75 = 1.8 square metres.

messages.content: At a Mangaluru lunch, volunteers pour 3.75 litres of buttermilk into 250 ml tumblers. How many tumblers can be filled?
15 tumblers can be filled.
messages.think:
The available volume is 3.75 × 1000 = 3750 ml.
It fills 3750 / 250 = 15 tumblers.

messages.content: A training session at Aizawl takes 80 minutes. The briefing uses 26 minutes. How much time is left for practice?
54 minutes are left for practice.
messages.think: After briefing, practice can take 80 - 26 = 54 minutes.

messages.content: In Ujjain a vendor sets out six baskets of 23 lemons. Twelve lemons are bruised. She packs the good ones in bags of nine. How many complete bags can she make?
She can make 14 complete bags.
messages.think:
The baskets hold 6 × 23 = 138 lemons.
Sorting leaves 138 - 12 = 126 good lemons.
Bags of nine account for 126 / 9 = 14 complete bags.

messages.content: In Salur, Pranav leaves at 4:53, spends 11 minutes walking to the bus and reaches his stop 26 minutes later. What time does he get off?
Pranav gets off at 5:30.
messages.think:
The two legs take 11 + 26 = 37 minutes.
Five o'clock comes after 60 - 53 = 7 minutes.
The rest of the journey takes 37 - 7 = 30 minutes after five.

messages.content: A Haridwar shop sells a lamp marked 1750 rupees at 14% off and charges 85 rupees for delivery. What total is payable?
The total payable is 1590 rupees.
messages.think:
The requested discount is 1750 × 14 / 100 = 245 rupees.
The lamp now costs 1750 - 245 = 1505 rupees.
With delivery the buyer pays 1505 + 85 = 1590.

messages.content: A Surat hostel office had 690 rupees in its UPI wallet. Four taxi charges of 86 rupees were debited, then a driver returned 24 rupees for an earlier overcharge. What does the wallet hold now?
The wallet now holds 370 rupees.
messages.think:
The new fares take out 4 × 86 = 344 rupees.
Before the refund the wallet holds 690 - 344 = 346.
The driver's credit brings it to 346 + 24 = 370.

messages.content: A Patna lab orders 160 slides. On Tuesday it receives 30% and on Wednesday another 32. What percentage of the order remains undelivered?
50% of the order remains undelivered.
messages.think:
Tuesday brings 160 × 30 / 100 = 48 slides.
After Wednesday the office has received 48 + 32 = 80.
The undelivered count is 160 - 80 = 80.
Its share of the order is 80 / 160 × 100 = 50 percent.

messages.content: A Siliguri play group has 72 gloves in a 5:4 ratio of green to purple. Seven purple gloves are lent out. How many purple gloves are left?
The group has 25 purple gloves left.
messages.think:
The ratio has 5 + 4 = 9 shares.
A share represents 72 / 9 = 8 gloves.
Purple accounts for 4 × 8 = 32 gloves at first.
The loan leaves 32 - 7 = 25.

messages.content: A Warangal room has a 9 m by 4 m wall with a 2 m by 1.5 m window. At 34 rupees per square metre, what is the cost of painting the wall around the window?
Painting costs 1122 rupees.
messages.think:
The wall rectangle covers 9 × 4 = 36 square metres.
The window takes 2 × 1.5 = 3 square metres.
Paint goes on 36 - 3 = 33 square metres.
The price for that area is 33 × 34 = 1122 rupees.

messages.content: A Roorkee shop pays 42 rupees per kg for 14 kg of rice and 57 rupees per kg for 6 kg. Find the average buying price per kg.
The average buying price is 46.5 rupees per kg.
messages.think:
The first purchase costs 14 × 42 = 588 rupees.
The second costs 6 × 57 = 342 rupees.
Together they cost 588 + 342 = 930.
The shop receives 14 + 6 = 20 kg.
The rate across both purchases is 930 / 20 = 46.5 rupees per kg.

messages.content: On a school outing in Churu, 60 pupils travel in three vans. The first two take 22 each. The final van has 19 seats. How many seats stay empty in it?
3 seats stay empty in the final van.
messages.think:
The full vans carry 2 × 22 = 44 pupils.
The last van carries 60 - 44 = 16 pupils.
That leaves 19 - 16 = 3 empty seats.

messages.content: At a Bidar community garden, a 580-litre tank starts at 195 litres. A tap delivers 28 litres a minute for eight minutes, then watering uses 63 litres. What volume can still be added?
Another 224 litres can be added.
messages.think:
The tap contributes 8 × 28 = 224 litres.
Before watering there are 195 + 224 = 419 litres.
Watering leaves 419 - 63 = 356 litres.
The remaining room in the tank is 580 - 356 = 224 litres.

messages.content: At a craft week in Panaji, access costs 96 rupees each day or 360 for a five-day pass. Dinesh plans to attend four days. Which choice saves money, and how much?
The five-day pass saves Dinesh 24 rupees.
messages.think:
The longer pass includes 5 - 4 = 1 unused day.
Separate passes cost 4 × 96 = 384 rupees.
The longer pass still saves 384 - 360 = 24 rupees.

messages.content: A Dharwad bindery has seven days to repair 140 books. It finishes 18 per day for the first three days and 20 on the fourth. It wants equal output on the remaining days. What daily figure should it aim for?
The bindery should aim for 22 books per day.
messages.think:
The first three days account for 3 × 18 = 54 books.
Day four lifts the repaired count to 54 + 20 = 74.
The outstanding count is 140 - 74 = 66.
The workshop has 7 - 4 = 3 days remaining.
It needs 66 / 3 = 22 books per day.

messages.content: A Mandya customer pays 1940 rupees, of which 140 is delivery. The bicycle stand itself was 25% off. What was its original price?
The stand was originally priced at 2400 rupees.
messages.think:
The actual price of the stand is 1940 - 140 = 1800 rupees.
That is 100 - 25 = 75 percent of its original price.
The original price is 1800 / 75 × 100 = 2400.

messages.content: The drama club in Ajmer needs 154 paper wristbands. One cupboard holds 42 and another holds 32. A shop sells packets of 16. How many should the club buy?
The club should buy 5 packets.
messages.think:
Its existing supply is 42 + 32 = 74 wristbands.
It still needs 154 - 74 = 80.
The required purchase is 80 / 16 = 5 packets.

messages.content: A driver travels 57 km in 1.5 hours on the way out of Nanded and another 135 km in 2.5 hours. What is the average speed for the four hours of driving?
The average speed is 48 km per hour.
messages.think:
The car covers 57 + 135 = 192 km.
Driving takes 1.5 + 2.5 = 4 hours.
The average speed is 192 / 4 = 48 km per hour.

messages.content: Three friends at a fair in Baramati split a 1230-rupee room and a 180-rupee ride equally. Each buys a 65-rupee entry pass. What does one friend spend?
One friend spends 535 rupees.
messages.think:
Their entry passes cost 3 × 65 = 195 rupees in all.
The total spend is 1230 + 180 + 195 = 1605 rupees.
Their equal individual expenses come to 1605 / 3 = 535 rupees each.

messages.content: A Jorhat science quiz gives 8 points for every correct answer and takes 3 off for every mistake. Blank answers are zero. Pahi has 11 correct, 5 wrong and 4 blank. What does she score?
Pahi scores 73 points.
messages.think:
Correct answers bring 11 × 8 = 88 points.
Wrong answers take away 5 × 3 = 15 points.
The blanks leave the score at 88 - 15 = 73.

messages.content: Samar is ninth in line at a Rewa bus enquiry desk. It reopens in 7 minutes. After opening, each customer ahead of Samar takes 4 minutes. When will he be served?
Samar will be served in 39 minutes.
messages.think:
There are 9 - 1 = 8 people ahead of Samar.
They will take 8 × 4 = 32 minutes.
Including the closure, he waits 7 + 32 = 39 minutes.

messages.content: A Belagavi kitchen has 4.8 kg of semolina and uses 1.2 kg in the morning and 950 grams later. How many grams remain?
2650 grams of semolina remain.
messages.think:
The pantry starts with 4.8 × 1000 = 4800 grams.
Morning cooking uses 1.2 × 1000 = 1200 grams.
Total use is 1200 + 950 = 2150 grams.
The unused amount is 4800 - 2150 = 2650 grams.

messages.content: Seven crates of grapes in Nashik weigh 26 kg each including their 2 kg crates. The vendor reserves 20 kg of grapes for a grocer. How much fruit can go to the street stall?
148 kg of grapes can go to the stall.
messages.think:
Each load contains 26 - 2 = 24 kg of grapes.
The fruit across the crates weighs 7 × 24 = 168 kg.
The stall gets 168 - 20 = 148 kg.

messages.content: A Junagadh club chases 183 runs in 20 overs. It has 112 after 13 overs and adds 11 in the next over. What must it average from here?
The club must average 10 runs per over.
messages.think:
The score moves to 112 + 11 = 123 runs.
The innings has used 13 + 1 = 14 overs.
The club has 20 - 14 = 6 overs to bat.
Its target is still 183 - 123 = 60 runs away.
Over the remaining overs it needs 60 / 6 = 10 per over.

messages.content: A 16 m by 11 m flower bed in Jalandhar needs wire around its edges, apart from a 4 m gate. How much wire will be used?
50 metres of wire will be used.
messages.think:
Two adjacent sides span 16 + 11 = 27 metres.
All four sides span 2 × 27 = 54 metres.
Leaving only the gate open reduces the wire length to 54 - 4 = 50 metres.

messages.content: A Kozhikode bakery makes 98 buns. It sets aside 11 for sampling and puts the rest into packets of 8. How many full packets and loose buns will it have?
It will have 10 full packets and 7 loose buns.
messages.think:
After sampling the available stock is 98 - 11 = 87 buns.
Ten full packets hold 10 × 8 = 80 buns.
The remaining count is 87 - 80 = 7, too few to fill another packet.

messages.content: In Chikmagalur a guest pays 920 rupees per night for the first two nights and 1180 for the third. A 650-rupee advance counts toward the bill. What is the checkout balance?
The checkout balance is 2370 rupees.
messages.think:
The first two nights total 2 × 920 = 1840 rupees.
All three cost 1840 + 1180 = 3020 rupees.
The advance leaves a balance of 3020 - 650 = 2370.

messages.content: At a Raichur shop, 13 plastic folders cost 28 rupees each and 5 clips cost 9 rupees each. Two torn folders are returned at the original price. What does the customer spend after the refund?
The customer spends 353 rupees after the refund.
messages.think:
The initial folder charge is 13 × 28 = 364 rupees.
The clip charge is 5 × 9 = 45 rupees.
The refund is 2 × 28 = 56 rupees.
The net payment is 364 + 45 - 56 = 353.

messages.content: A Surat workshop has 114 wooden discs and 96 brass rings. It reserves 18 discs and gives away one-quarter of the rings. Each ornament needs 4 discs and 3 rings. It sells as many complete ornaments as it can at 65 rupees each, and string costs 9 rupees per ornament. How much remains after the string expense?
1344 rupees remain after paying for string.
messages.think:
The available discs number 114 - 18 = 96.
The giveaway uses 96 / 4 = 24 rings.
That leaves 96 - 24 = 72 rings.
The discs will cover 96 / 4 = 24 ornaments.
The rings also cover 72 / 3 = 24 ornaments.
Each ornament nets 65 - 9 = 56 rupees after string.
All the ornaments net 24 × 56 = 1344 rupees after string.

messages.content: A group in Jodhpur books eight festival seats at 300 rupees each and pays a single 120-rupee booking fee. When three people cancel, the organiser returns their fares minus 80 rupees per cancelled seat and keeps the whole fee. If the five attendees split the final cost evenly, what is each share?
Each attendee pays 372 rupees.
messages.think:
The original fares come to 8 × 300 = 2400 rupees.
The fee raises the amount paid to 2400 + 120 = 2520.
The cancelled seat fares total 3 × 300 = 900 rupees.
Cancellation deductions total 3 × 80 = 240.
The refund is 900 - 240 = 660 rupees.
The expense after the refund is 2520 - 660 = 1860 rupees.
Each attendee contributes 1860 / 5 = 372 rupees.

messages.content: A Nainital lodge wants to coat a 30 m by 14 m roof, leaving a 5 m by 4 m shed and a separate 10 m by 4 m strip around the skylights alone. A litre covers 8 square metres. The foreman wants 20% extra. How many 6-litre tins are needed?
The foreman needs 9 tins.
messages.think:
The full roof measures 30 × 14 = 420 square metres.
The shed covers 5 × 4 = 20 square metres.
The other excluded strip measures 10 × 4 = 40 square metres.
Coating goes on 420 - 20 - 40 = 360 square metres.
Coverage needs 360 / 8 = 45 litres.
The extra material is 45 × 20 / 100 = 9 litres.
The purchase must cover 45 + 9 = 54 litres.
The tins needed number 54 / 6 = 9.

messages.content: A family in Mahabalipuram books four nights at 1350 rupees a night. The hotel gives 15% off the room bill. They buy seven breakfasts at 140 rupees each. Of a refundable 500-rupee deposit, the hotel keeps 75 rupees for a lost key. What is the family's net spend?
The family spends 5645 rupees after the refund.
messages.think:
Four nights start at 4 × 1350 = 5400 rupees.
The room discount comes to 5400 × 15 / 100 = 810.
The reduced room charge is 5400 - 810 = 4590 rupees.
Breakfasts cost 7 × 140 = 980 rupees.
The refundable part of the deposit is 500 - 75 = 425 rupees.
The net bill is 4590 + 980 + 500 - 425 = 5645 rupees.

messages.content: At a Ramanagara workshop, Ali can label 21 boxes per hour and Francis 15. Ali works alone for two hours, then they work together for three. After a 20-minute break Francis finishes the 175-box order alone. How long from the start until completion?
The order takes 420 minutes from start to finish.
messages.think:
Ali labels 2 × 21 = 42 boxes alone.
Together the two can label 21 + 15 = 36 boxes per hour.
Their joint stint labels 3 × 36 = 108 boxes.
The final stint must cover 175 - 42 - 108 = 25 boxes.
Francis takes 25 / 15 × 60 = 100 minutes to finish.
The first two stints last 2 × 60 + 3 × 60 = 300 minutes.
Adding the break gives 300 + 20 + 100 = 420 minutes.

messages.content: A drink seller in Sivasagar blends 1.6 litres of a drink containing 30% lemon juice with 900 ml of a drink containing 60% lemon juice. She adds 500 ml of water. Assuming volumes add directly, what percentage of the result is lemon juice?
The result is 34% lemon juice.
messages.think:
The first drink measures 1.6 × 1000 = 1600 ml.
It contains 1600 × 30 / 100 = 480 ml of juice.
The second drink contains 900 × 60 / 100 = 540 ml of juice.
The combined juice is 480 + 540 = 1020 ml.
After adding water the liquid measures 1600 + 900 + 500 = 3000 ml.
The percentage is 1020 / 3000 × 100 = 34.

messages.content: A theatre in Bathinda starts with 13 rows of 14 chairs. A sound desk takes the space of two rows. Staff add four rows of nine chairs and reserve 18 chairs for volunteers. There are 203 other people to seat. If a bench seats six, what is the minimum number of benches needed?
Bring in at least 6 benches.
messages.think:
The original layout holds 13 × 14 = 182 chairs.
The sound desk removes 2 × 14 = 28 chairs.
The original seating drops to 182 - 28 = 154 chairs.
The new rows bring 4 × 9 = 36 chairs.
The resulting layout has 154 + 36 = 190 chairs.
General seating after reservations is 190 - 18 = 172 chairs.
The shortage is 203 - 172 = 31 places.
Five benches give 5 × 6 = 30 places, so 5 + 1 = 6 benches are needed.

messages.content: A Guntur mill uses 310 electricity units. Its contract charges 4 rupees for each of the first 90 units, 6 for each of the next 110 units and 8 for each unit thereafter. A monthly charge of 165 rupees applies, and the mill has a 65-rupee credit. What does it owe?
The mill owes 2000 rupees.
messages.think:
The first band costs 90 × 4 = 360 rupees.
The second band costs 110 × 6 = 660 rupees.
The upper band covers 310 - 90 - 110 = 110 units.
Those units cost 110 × 8 = 880 rupees.
Before the credit the bill totals 360 + 660 + 880 + 165 = 2065 rupees.
Applying the credit leaves 2065 - 65 = 2000 rupees due.

messages.content: A Kanpur shop records average sales of 32 diaries per day over five days. It wrote 26 for a day that actually had 39 sales and double-counted three sales on another day. On day six it sells 40 diaries. What is the corrected average across all six days?
The corrected average is 35 diaries per day.
messages.think:
The book implies 5 × 32 = 160 sales at first.
The understated day is missing 39 - 26 = 13 sales.
Repairing that entry gives 160 + 13 = 173 sales.
Removing duplicates drops the count to 173 - 3 = 170 sales.
Day six raises the total to 170 + 40 = 210.
The average is 210 / 6 = 35 diaries per day.

messages.content: A festival committee in Udupi plans 14 rows of lamps. The first row has 5 and every following row uses two more than the previous one. A separate entrance display uses 15 lamps on each side. The committee has 49 lamps in storage and can buy boxes of 20. How many boxes should it buy?
The committee should buy 12 boxes.
messages.think:
The final row is reached after 14 - 1 = 13 increases.
The final row uses 5 + 13 × 2 = 31 lamps.
The outer pair uses 5 + 31 = 36, and moving both rows inward adds two to one and takes two from the other.
The matched rows therefore use 14 / 2 × 36 = 252 lamps.
The entrance adds 2 × 15 = 30 lamps.
The combined arrangement needs 252 + 30 = 282 lamps.
Storage reduces the purchase requirement to 282 - 49 = 233 lamps.
Eleven boxes supply 11 × 20 = 220, which falls short, so buy 11 + 1 = 12 boxes.

messages.content: At a Solapur craft stall, Jaya pays for an 83-rupee sketchbook with a 100-rupee note. What change should she get?
Jaya should get 17 rupees back.
messages.think: The change is the difference 100 - 83 = 17.

messages.content: A Narasaraopet school has six cupboards with 14 mats in each. How many mats does it have?
It has 84 mats.
messages.think: The identical stocks give 6 × 14 = 84 mats.

messages.content: A club in Bijnor distributes 108 badges evenly among nine classes. What is a class's share?
Each class gets 12 badges.
messages.think: The equal portions are 108 / 9 = 12 badges each.

messages.content: A boat in Karwar loads cargo between 7:12 and 7:46. How long does the loading last?
Loading lasts 34 minutes.
messages.think: Both times lie within the same hour, so 46 - 12 = 34 minutes.

messages.content: In Mahad, Ani cuts two lengths of string measuring 0.85 and 2.4 metres. What is their combined length?
Their combined length is 3.25 metres.
messages.think: Placed end to end, they measure 0.85 + 2.4 = 3.25 metres.

messages.content: A garden shop in Bundi discounts a 560-rupee trimmer by 15%. How much money does that take off?
The discount takes off 84 rupees.
messages.think: The amount taken off is 560 × 15 / 100 = 84.

messages.content: A Salem cook has 2.25 kg of jaggery and uses 650 grams. Give the remaining weight in grams.
1600 grams of jaggery remain.
messages.think:
The initial weight is 2.25 × 1000 = 2250 grams.
Cooking leaves 2250 - 650 = 1600 grams.

messages.content: At a Srikakulam school, the office issues 25 visitor slips on Monday and 18 on Tuesday. How many were issued across those days?
The office issued 43 slips.
messages.think: The two days' issue count is 25 + 18 = 43.

messages.content: Miki walks 950 metres to a bookshop in Aizawl and another 650 metres to a café. How far is that in kilometres?
Miki walks 1.6 kilometres.
messages.think:
Both legs cover 950 + 650 = 1600 metres.
In kilometres that is 1600 / 1000 = 1.6.

messages.content: Four kachoris cost 16 rupees apiece at a Kota stall. The vendor charges 5 rupees for a box. What is the total?
The total is 69 rupees.
messages.think:
The kachoris cost 4 × 16 = 64 rupees.
The box brings the bill to 64 + 5 = 69.

messages.content: A Nagapattinam storytelling session has a 70-minute slot. The first story takes 26 minutes. How much time is available for the others?
The other stories have 44 minutes.
messages.think: The remaining slot lasts 70 - 26 = 44 minutes.

messages.content: During a Rang Panchami event in Indore, a volunteer saves one-sixth of 84 paper flags for the gate. How many are saved?
14 flags are saved for the gate.
messages.think: One-sixth of the stock is 84 / 6 = 14 flags.

messages.content: An Idukki seedling bench is 2.2 metres long and 0.8 metres wide. What is the area of the top?
The bench top is 1.76 square metres.
messages.think: Its rectangular top covers 2.2 × 0.8 = 1.76 square metres.

messages.content: At a Khandwa canteen, 6.4 litres of drinking water is poured into 800 ml bottles. How many bottles can be filled to the top?
8 bottles can be filled to the top.
messages.think:
The available amount is 6.4 × 1000 = 6400 ml.
The number of full bottles is 6400 / 800 = 8.

messages.content: A clay artist in Bankura decorates 53 cups on Tuesday and 17 fewer on Wednesday. What is Wednesday's figure?
She decorates 36 cups on Wednesday.
messages.think: The smaller day's count is 53 - 17 = 36.

messages.content: In Buldhana, a delivery brings seven trays of 18 peaches. Six fruits are bruised. The shop packs good peaches in cartons of ten. How many can it fill?
The shop can fill 12 cartons.
messages.think:
The delivery contains 7 × 18 = 126 peaches.
Sorting leaves 126 - 6 = 120 good peaches.
The available stock fills 120 / 10 = 12 cartons.

messages.content: Pema leaves a school office in Gangtok at 3:51. She walks 18 minutes to the market and another 16 to her house. When does she arrive?
Pema arrives at 4:25.
messages.think:
Her walk takes 18 + 16 = 34 minutes.
The hour changes after 60 - 51 = 9 minutes.
Home is another 34 - 9 = 25 minutes into the next hour.

messages.content: A screen in Shivamogga is marked 2400 rupees. The dealer gives 18% off, then adds 132 rupees for installation. What must the buyer pay?
The buyer must pay 2100 rupees.
messages.think:
The discount is 2400 × 18 / 100 = 432 rupees.
The screen costs 2400 - 432 = 1968 rupees before installation.
Fitting it raises the bill to 1968 + 132 = 2100.

messages.content: A Vadodara student has 660 rupees on her bus card. She takes three rides at 68 rupees and one at 44 rupees. What is left?
The card has 412 rupees left.
messages.think:
The repeated fare uses 3 × 68 = 204 rupees.
The total debit is 204 + 44 = 248.
The card retains 660 - 248 = 412.

messages.content: A hall in Talcher orders 175 folding chairs. The supplier brings 20% one day and 70 the next. What percentage remains due?
40% of the order remains due.
messages.think:
The first delivery contains 175 × 20 / 100 = 35 chairs.
Two deliveries provide 35 + 70 = 105 chairs.
There is a shortfall of 175 - 105 = 70 chairs.
The order is still 70 / 175 × 100 = 40 percent unfilled.

messages.content: At a Dausa workshop, 90 spools of blue and red thread are in the ratio 4:5. A tailor takes 11 red spools. How many red spools are left?
39 red spools are left.
messages.think:
The ratio is made of 4 + 5 = 9 shares.
One share contains 90 / 9 = 10 spools.
Red starts at 5 × 10 = 50 spools.
After the tailor's visit, 50 - 11 = 39 red spools remain.

messages.content: A Buxar reading room has a 9 m by 3 m wall. A 2 m by 2 m poster must stay in place. Painting the exposed area costs 48 rupees per square metre. What is the bill?
The painting bill is 1104 rupees.
messages.think:
The wall has 9 × 3 = 27 square metres.
The poster takes up 2 × 2 = 4 square metres.
The painter covers 27 - 4 = 23 square metres.
The quoted price gives 23 × 48 = 1104 rupees.

messages.content: A vendor in Erode buys 12 kg of dried chilli at 95 rupees per kg and 8 kg at 70 rupees per kg. What average price per kg does she pay?
She pays an average of 85 rupees per kg.
messages.think:
The first lot costs 12 × 95 = 1140 rupees.
The second lot costs 8 × 70 = 560 rupees.
The purchase totals 1140 + 560 = 1700 rupees.
The two weights add to 12 + 8 = 20 kg.
The average is 1700 / 20 = 85 rupees per kg.

messages.content: A Balasore excursion has 55 people in three vehicles. The first two vehicles take 18 people each. The third has 23 seats. How many seats remain free in it?
There are 4 free seats in the third vehicle.
messages.think:
The first pair takes 2 × 18 = 36 people.
The final vehicle takes 55 - 36 = 19 people.
Its unused capacity is 23 - 19 = 4 seats.

messages.content: At a Jalna site, a 600-litre tank holds 160 litres. A pump adds 35 litres a minute for eight minutes. Workers use 70 litres. How many more litres will fill the tank?
Another 230 litres will fill the tank.
messages.think:
The pump supplies 8 × 35 = 280 litres.
The amount before use is 160 + 280 = 440 litres.
Work leaves 440 - 70 = 370 litres.
The volume still needed is 600 - 370 = 230 litres.

messages.content: A Panipat exhibition sells daily passes for 79 rupees or a five-day pass for 300. Deepa will attend four days. Which option saves money, and how much?
The five-day pass saves 16 rupees.
messages.think:
The five-day pass has 5 - 4 = 1 unused day.
Four separate passes cost 4 × 79 = 316 rupees.
The five-day pass saves 316 - 300 = 16 rupees.

messages.content: A Udupi bakery has six days to prepare 108 gift boxes. The first three days produce 18 boxes apiece and the fourth produces 16. How many per day are needed on the last two days for an even finish?
Prepare 19 boxes on each of the last two days.
messages.think:
The first three days supply 3 × 18 = 54 boxes.
Through day four production is 54 + 16 = 70 boxes.
The unfinished quantity is 108 - 70 = 38.
The last two days each need 38 / 2 = 19.

messages.content: A Jhansi customer pays 1910 rupees for a cabinet with delivery. Delivery costs 110 rupees, and the cabinet was sold at 25% off. What was its marked price?
The marked price was 2400 rupees.
messages.think:
The cabinet alone cost 1910 - 110 = 1800 rupees.
The sale took 100 - 25 = 75 percent of the marked price.
The full price is 1800 / 75 × 100 = 2400 rupees.

messages.content: A neighbourhood event in Ponda requires 168 name tags. The organiser has 35 at home and finds another 49 at the hall. Shop packs hold 14 each. How many packs does the organiser need?
The organiser needs 6 packs.
messages.think:
The two sources provide 35 + 49 = 84 tags.
Purchases must cover 168 - 84 = 84 more.
The pack count is 84 / 14 = 6.

messages.content: A driver leaving Kangra covers 49 km in 1.5 hours and then 111 km in 2.5 hours. Find the average driving speed for both legs.
The average speed is 40 km per hour.
messages.think:
The route measures 49 + 111 = 160 km.
It takes 1.5 + 2.5 = 4 hours of driving.
The whole-drive average is 160 / 4 = 40 km per hour.

messages.content: Four friends in Bhuj split a room costing 1360 rupees and a shared ride costing 260. Each also pays 95 rupees for entry. What does each spend?
Each friend spends 500 rupees.
messages.think:
All entries cost 4 × 95 = 380 rupees.
The group's expense is 1360 + 260 + 380 = 2000 rupees.
Each contributes 2000 / 4 = 500 rupees.

messages.content: A Himatnagar quiz awards 8 points per correct answer, deducts 4 per mistake and gives zero for a blank. Jinal gets 13 correct, four wrong and three blank. What is her score?
Jinal scores 88 points.
messages.think:
Correct answers bring in 13 × 8 = 104 points.
Mistakes cost 4 × 4 = 16 points.
Blanks have no effect, so her score is 104 - 16 = 88.

messages.content: Bishal is eighth in the Tezpur ticket queue. The counter opens in 9 minutes and each customer ahead of him takes 6 minutes. When does his turn start?
Bishal's turn starts in 51 minutes.
messages.think:
Ahead of Bishal are 8 - 1 = 7 customers.
Serving them takes 7 × 6 = 42 minutes.
Including the closed period, his wait is 9 + 42 = 51 minutes.

messages.content: A Vijayapura kitchen has 5.6 kg of rice in the morning. It uses 1.25 kg for lunch and 950 grams for dinner. Find the unused weight in grams.
3400 grams remain unused.
messages.think:
The opening quantity is 5.6 × 1000 = 5600 grams.
Lunch uses 1.25 × 1000 = 1250 grams.
Total use is 1250 + 950 = 2200 grams.
The remainder is 5600 - 2200 = 3400 grams.

messages.content: At a Burdwan depot, a full crate weighs 26 kg and an empty one weighs 2 kg. There are nine full crates. The depot retains 18 kg of the vegetables and dispatches the rest. What weight is dispatched?
The depot dispatches 198 kg of vegetables.
messages.think:
Vegetables per crate weigh 26 - 2 = 24 kg.
Total vegetable weight is 9 × 24 = 216 kg.
After retention the depot dispatches 216 - 18 = 198 kg.

messages.content: A cricket club in Rohtak chases 169 runs in 19 overs. It reaches 99 at the end of over 12 and hits 16 in over 13. What rate does it need over the remaining overs?
The club needs 9 runs per over.
messages.think:
The latest score is 99 + 16 = 115.
Overs used are 12 + 1 = 13.
The club has 19 - 13 = 6 overs left.
It still needs 169 - 115 = 54 runs.
The required rate is 54 / 6 = 9 runs an over.

messages.content: A nursery in Palakkad will fence a rectangle 22 m by 14 m. A 3 m gap must remain at its entrance. How much fencing is required?
The nursery needs 69 metres of fencing.
messages.think:
One long and one short side total 22 + 14 = 36 metres.
The perimeter is 2 × 36 = 72 metres.
Subtracting the entry gap gives 72 - 3 = 69.

messages.content: A Dindigul producer makes 91 snack bars and sets eight aside for staff. It fills packets with nine bars each. How many full packets and loose bars does it get?
It gets 9 full packets and 2 loose bars.
messages.think:
The packing table receives 91 - 8 = 83 bars.
Nine full packets use 9 × 9 = 81 bars.
The loose count is 83 - 81 = 2, below another packet's capacity.

messages.content: A Kanyakumari homestay charges 980 rupees per night for two nights and 1120 for the third. A guest has already paid 700 rupees towards the room. What remains due?
2380 rupees remain due.
messages.think:
The first two nights cost 2 × 980 = 1960 rupees.
The charge for the full stay is 1960 + 1120 = 3080 rupees.
The amount due is 3080 - 700 = 2380 rupees.

messages.content: In Hardoi, Anas buys 12 chalk holders at 27 rupees each and five tins at 16 each. The shop refunds two faulty holders in full. How much does he ultimately spend?
Anas ultimately spends 350 rupees.
messages.think:
The original holder charge is 12 × 27 = 324 rupees.
The tins cost 5 × 16 = 80 rupees.
The shop returns 2 × 27 = 54 rupees.
Net spending is 324 + 80 - 54 = 350 rupees.

messages.content: Two schools in Nanded have waiting lists of 34 and 42 pupils for a science show. The theatre holds 190, but 18 seats are reserved for staff and 97 pupils already have tickets. The first school gets 60% of the seats available to the waiting lists. The second school gets all seats the first school does not use. How many pupils from each list still need seats?
No pupils remain on the first list, and 1 pupil remains on the second.
messages.think:
Pupil capacity is 190 - 18 = 172 seats.
The waiting lists can use 172 - 97 = 75 seats.
The planned allocation for the first school is 75 × 60 / 100 = 45 seats.
The first school uses only 34, so it gives back 45 - 34 = 11 seats.
The second school can use 75 - 45 + 11 = 41 seats.
The remaining demand is 34 - 34 = 0 at the first school and 42 - 41 = 1 at the second.

messages.content: A co-operative in Palanpur delivers 250 kg of grain. Its contract pays 36 rupees per kg for up to 180 kg and 30 per kg for the excess. The buyer rejects 10 kg before pricing. Transport costs 650 rupees. Separately, a member prepays a quarter of that transport cost, so the co-operative pays only the rest. What amount remains from the sale after the co-operative's own transport expense?
The co-operative retains 7792 rupees and 50 paise.
messages.think:
The buyer accepts 250 - 10 = 240 kg.
The first price band brings 180 × 36 = 6480 rupees.
The second band applies to 240 - 180 = 60 kg.
This adds 60 × 30 = 1800 rupees.
The member covers 650 / 4 = 162.5 rupees of transport.
The co-operative pays 650 - 162.5 = 487.5 rupees for transport.
The proceeds remaining are 6480 + 1800 - 487.5 = 7792.5 rupees.

messages.content: A music group in Mysuru starts with 120 drum straps and 98 buckles. It tests 20 straps and finds that all 20 are unusable. Ten buckles go to another class. Four straps and four buckles are used in each finished set. The sets are sold for 160 rupees each, and the group must pay 210 rupees stall rent and 8 rupees for packaging every set. How much remains from the sale?
3134 rupees remain from the sale.
messages.think:
There are 120 - 20 = 100 usable straps.
There are 98 - 10 = 88 buckles available.
The straps can supply 100 / 4 = 25 sets.
The buckles can supply 88 / 4 = 22 sets, so they limit production to 22.
Sales bring in 22 × 160 = 3520 rupees.
Packaging and rent together cost 22 × 8 + 210 = 386 rupees.
After those charges, 3520 - 386 = 3134 rupees remain.

messages.content: A Madurai stage crew has 16 metres of black fabric and 14 metres of blue fabric. They set aside 2 metres of black and 80 cm of blue for repairs, then make panels that each need 50 cm of black and 55 cm of blue. They sell six panels to another troupe and install the rest in equal numbers across three entrances. How many go at each entrance?
Install 6 panels at each entrance.
messages.think:
The usable black length is 16 - 2 = 14 metres.
Converted to centimetres it measures 14 × 100 = 1400.
The available blue fabric measures 14 × 100 - 80 = 1320 cm.
The black fabric can cover 1400 / 50 = 28 panels.
The blue fabric can cover 1320 / 55 = 24 panels, so only 24 are made.
The sale leaves 24 - 6 = 18 for the stage crew.
Dividing among three entrances gives 18 / 3 = 6 each.

messages.content: In Guwahati, a community group prepares a 26 m by 16 m courtyard for a food fair. A separate 5 m by 4 m platform and a 6 m by 6 m play area remain bare. Covering the rest takes one roll per 10 square metres. It wants 10% more coverage than the area calls for and already has four full rolls. How many whole rolls should it buy?
The group should buy 36 whole rolls.
messages.think:
The courtyard covers 26 × 16 = 416 square metres.
The platform takes 5 × 4 = 20 square metres.
The play area takes 6 × 6 = 36 square metres.
The remaining area is 416 - 20 - 36 = 360 square metres.
Regular coverage needs 360 / 10 = 36 roll equivalents.
Allowing extra needs 36 + 36 × 10 / 100 = 39.6 roll equivalents.
After existing stock, 39.6 - 4 = 35.6 roll equivalents are missing.
That exceeds the coverage of 35 rolls, so buy 35 + 1 = 36 rolls.

messages.content: The makers at a Patan workshop earn 35 rupees per notebook. Kavya starts with a two-hour solo stint at 18 notebooks per hour. A second maker joins at 22 per hour, and they work together for 90 minutes. The next day they sell every notebook at that price and pay 11 rupees each for materials and a flat 300-rupee stall fee. What stays with the workshop?
The workshop retains 2004 rupees.
messages.think:
The solo stint provides 2 × 18 = 36 notebooks.
Their combined rate is 18 + 22 = 40 notebooks an hour.
The shared time is 90 / 60 = 1.5 hours.
The pair adds 1.5 × 40 = 60 notebooks.
The full sale count is 36 + 60 = 96.
Each sale leaves 35 - 11 = 24 rupees after materials.
After rent the workshop retains 96 × 24 - 300 = 2004 rupees.

messages.content: A music teacher in Alwar bought 80 matching bells. She returned 12 faulty bells at their full price of 30 rupees each. Of the good bells, she gives 8 away and sells the others at 55 rupees each. An assistant earns a commission of 5% of the sales. Once the refund, sales and commission are all included, how much more money does she have than before the original purchase?
She has 1095 rupees more than before the purchase.
messages.think:
Buying the batch costs 80 × 30 = 2400 rupees.
The faulty items bring back 12 × 30 = 360 rupees.
The number sold is 80 - 12 - 8 = 60 bells.
Gross sales are 60 × 55 = 3300 rupees.
The commission is 3300 × 5 / 100 = 165 rupees.
Her cash gain is 360 + 3300 - 2400 - 165 = 1095 rupees.

messages.content: In Durgapur a shuttle operator charges 140 rupees for the first 8 km, then 13 rupees per km for the next 12 km and 18 rupees per km beyond that. On a 27 km trip there is a 52-rupee toll. The fare alone is discounted by 10%. A client pays 100 rupees upfront towards the bill. What balance is due?
